**Triage: duplicate of #6088 — closing. Same 7 advisories, seen through a different reporting channel.**

This issue registers the Dependabot banner (`7 vulnerabilities: 2 high, 4 moderate, 1 low`). #6088, filed 17 minutes earlier at 00:15:59Z from the osv-scanner side (`Validate Package Dependencies`, run 31132523916), enumerates the full advisory table. The two counts reconcile exactly:

| GHSA | CVSS | GitHub severity | package | current | patched |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| GHSA-5p4m-2wfm-xmqj | 7.5 | **high** | js-yaml | 3.15.0 | 3.15.1 |
| GHSA-5p4m-2wfm-xmqj | 7.5 | **high** | js-yaml | 4.3.0 | 4.3.1 |
| GHSA-3rrr-jr9j-h3q3 | 6.5 | moderate | mermaid | 11.16.0 | 11.16.1 |
| GHSA-2v8p-3f2j-5mp7 | 5.3 | moderate | mermaid | 11.16.0 | 11.16.1 |
| GHSA-6x64-9x62-f2gx | 5.3 | moderate | mermaid | 11.16.0 | 11.16.1 |
| GHSA-rhh3-jpg6-66xh | 5.3 | moderate | mermaid | 11.16.0 | 11.16.1 |
| GHSA-c4c3-pg64-4m4v | 2.4 | low | mermaid | 11.16.0 | 11.16.1 |

⇒ **2 high + 4 moderate + 1 low = 7**, matching this issue's banner exactly. The severity split is not a coincidence of totals: it is the CVSS→GitHub-severity mapping of #6088's seven rows, row for row.

**Independently verified against `origin/main` (`1eb13a0`), not taken from #6088's text.** The vulnerable versions are all present in the lockfile — `js-yaml@3.15.0`, `js-yaml@4.3.0`, `mermaid@11.16.0` (`js-yaml@4.0.9` / `@5.2.2` are also resolved but fall outside the advisory's ranges). Last lockfile commit is `9c90ea0` (`feat(sms)`, #6042) — no OSV remediation has landed, so both reports describe the same live state.

Note the triage seat could not read `GET /repos/.../dependabot/alerts` directly (403, `Resource not accessible by integration`), so the reconciliation above is by severity arithmetic + lockfile evidence rather than by pulling the alert list. If someone with Security-tab access finds an **eighth** alert outside this table, reopen — the arithmetic is exact but it is arithmetic.

**Why close rather than cross-link:** #6088 is already claimed and in flight (`pm:dispatched`, session `session_01Wbxm29qPKnLf44AbSxizqW`, branch `claude/issue-6088-osv-jsyaml-mermaid`, 00:30:52Z), and its declared file surface is `pnpm-lock.yaml`. A lockfile fix is the canonical never-parallelize surface — two re-resolutions produce mutually unmergeable diffs (the #5032 precedent). Leaving an unassigned second entry for the same lockfile bump is precisely the shape that invites a second claim, and this issue's own body asks only for grading and routing — work #6088 has already absorbed. One thing, one dispatch entry.

**Nothing carried over is lost.** This issue's three asks are all answered on #6088: ① the ranked list is its scan table above; ② routing — the lockfile is a shared-infrastructure surface, and the maintainer directed the `domain:cli` lane to take it (per the claim comment; the triage seat notes the fix touches no domain package, so no `domain:*` label is warranted on a pure lockfile bump — recorded here rather than relabelling someone else's in-flight issue); ③ the "batch upgrade" shape is what #6088 is dispatched as — all seven have patch-level fixes.

Maintainer may veto this closure by reopening; no restart condition is needed because the surviving issue carries the work.
